query:
The group operates with an expectation that everyone contributes something — food or a game — to shared sessions and events. Based on the conversations, does this expectation apply to every member? If not, who approaches it differently and what does the conversation show about their actual practice?

Options:
A. Nadia
B. Soo-Yeon
C. Raj
D. Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Lena, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:05:00) so basically the norm here is bring something, game or food, agreed tbh. one could argue that even the people who brought nothing last year understood this expectation, they just didn't follow through
[2] (about=Marcus, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:03:00) The rule is bring a game or bring food. Both is ideal. Enforcement is just social pressure.
[3] (about=Lena, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:24:00) Priya you mentioned a relational disclosure earlier that I wanted to follow up on tbh. you and Derek seem to have different vibes about the session energy. like i've noticed he tends to go quiet when cooperative options are even mentioned?
[4] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:04:00) In my experience the marathon only works when everyone contributes. It is the social contract of a shared day.
agent_answer:
Based on the material, the expectation applies to every member: the norm is that everyone brings something — a game or food — and enforcement is just social pressure. This is stated as the group rule, and Tomasz also says everyone must contribute.

There is no evidence that any of the named options approaches it differently. Nadia, Soo-Yeon, Raj, and Marcus are all marked as having no record on this matter, and the raw excerpts do not link any of them to a different practice. The only mention of people who “brought nothing” last year is unnamed and does not identify whether any of these four were among them.

So: none of the options — Nadia, Soo-Yeon, Raj, or Marcus — is shown to approach the expectation differently.
